Medals

      
The salt clubs
Top speed anywhere out on the salt flats. Each club pays once.

      
The county's people
A column of light in someone's colour means they have work for you: stop beside them and listen. One job at a time. Three of them open a car at the dealer.

      
Challenges
A column of light marks where each one starts. Stop in it and press Enter (or Start), or pick one here to go straight to its line. Gold, silver and bronze pay the first time; a better medal later pays the difference, and a repeat pays a tenth.

    

    

      
How hard

      
Races
You race the car you're in, as it's built, against drivers in factory cars rated close to yours for that ground. The better you place, the more it pays.

    

    

      
The bay
Your car on the dyno as its Studio 2 (Drive ▶ takes it out onto the salt and the sand), the whole screen: the views, the hood up on the engine, and the engine on the lab's own sim. Drag to turn round it, over it and underneath; pinch or scroll to come closer; right-drag to slide along it.

Studio 2 is each build as it's modelled, so its body, tyres, wheels and ride height are its own: pick the build under Start from. The paint and everything under the skin are yours to change.

    Bests
    
      
    How the money works
    Every feat pays: drifts, jumps, two wheels, saving it from a roll, speed runs on dirt and gravel, burnouts, close calls past the trees, splashes, the mud pit, Red Hill, the rock garden, laps and clock runs. Do them back to back and they stack into a combo: the multiplier grows with every feat and more with every new kind. The combo banks after a few quiet seconds. Roll it, wreck it or reset before then and the unbanked money is gone.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Clock runs
    From one place to another, any way you like. The clock starts when you move. Beat the par time for a bonus.
    
      
    The race track
    Drive over the start line at the race track to start a lap.
    
    
    
    
    
      
    Cameras
        
    The camera button (C, or CAM on a phone) only goes through the cameras that are on. The Director switches between them by itself, holding each for its time. Jump cam cuts to a camera off to the side whenever the car takes off, and back once it lands.

    Sound
    
      
    The engine's sound
    The synth is the Digital Engine lab's, untouched: these change how it's heard. Like the bay hears it from the lab's spot 3 m behind, like the model bay; From the camera is how Dirt Sleeper HD did it. Fuller adds low end after the synth; Phone speaker lifts the low mids instead, if a phone's own speaker turns the deep bass into buzz.

    Pitch (V while driving)
    
          
    Keyboard gas
    
        
    Pitch is a test: the synth is told the engine turns 10 or 20% slower than it does, so the note drops; the tach, the shifts and the speed stay true. Keyboard gas: Like a foot is half gas while you hold W, so the automatic shifts around 3,500 like a truck driven normally; tap W twice quickly to floor it (a kickdown) until you let go; Floor it is all or nothing, every gear to the redline. 1 to 9 always give that much gas.

    The open world
    The town, the country and the salt, made in 128 m chunks round you as you drive and let go behind you. Cruise holds the road you're on (its right-hand lane) so you can watch the world come in. Brake to stop it.

    Developer: traction
    
      
    For tuning while the game is made; the finished game won't have this. Traction is the ground, not the cars. It sets how much grip each surface gives, and every car feels that through its own tyres, so the cars keep their order: on dirt the drag car's slicks have less grip than the crawler's mud tyres at any setting, and on the drag strip they have more. The handling knobs work on every car, each from its own setup. Changes take hold as you drive and are remembered. T while driving steps Traction through 75, 100, 125 and 150%.

    Developer: the look
    
      
    Judgment calls about the picture, to A/B on the phone. Each is a multiplier on what the time of day (or the studio) sets; 100% is the game as tuned against Wide Open's own pictures. Tell me the values you settle on and they become the defaults. Saved on this device.
    
      
    
      
    
      
    
    
    
    
    Developer: the phone's budgets
    
      
    What the world and the cars hand the renderer on the Mobile tier, to trim on the phone while the performance readout (F, or Numbers on screen: Readout, above) shows the frame time. The other tiers always draw everything. Saved on this device.
